### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**13** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f0e3acea404fe707d6f83f42b97f0d689bd5fdb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dac458fa739259c9f2a164e883a2885c83d14f6e` — the merge of head `93e3a44aa4f4c0116075f7189f57d1eafe709665` into base `3f0e3acea404fe707d6f83f42b97f0d689bd5fdb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dac458fa739259c9f2a164e883a2885c83d14f6e && git checkout dac458fa739259c9f2a164e883a2885c83d14f6e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f0e3acea404fe707d6f83f42b97f0d689bd5fdb 93e3a44aa4f4c0116075f7189f57d1eafe709665 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f0e3acea404fe707d6f83f42b97f0d689bd5fdb && git merge --no-ff 93e3a44aa4f4c0116075f7189f57d1eafe709665

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f0e3acea404fe707d6f83f42b97f0d689bd5fdb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `93e3a44aa4f4c0116075f7189f57d1eafe709665`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/cube-member-key.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/structured-json-dimension-door.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dotted-dimension-unbacked-join-parity.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-filter-field-binding.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/order-key-door.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md, content/docs/references/data/analytics.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx, packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (read, not reviewed)
Inputs: card #31842 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #31878 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's 47 check-runs at 2026-11-09T09:17Z: 42 concluded (success or skipped, no failure, none cancelled), 5 still `in_progress` (Test Core shards 1/8, 3/8, 4/8, 7/8, 8/8). Judged on what has concluded; `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, every `Type Check` job, every `Lint` job and the concluded Test Core shards are green. Not read: the dispatch order's conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing, filter / dimension / time-dimension members — right.** `declaredCubeMemberKey` (cube-member-key.ts) resolves a dotted spelling to a declared key only verbatim, behind the cube's own qualifier (`cube.name`, or the bare object `cube.sql` names), or through an underscore-flattened key whose own `sql` is the same relationship path. The bare-tail arm (`if (bag[tail]) return bag[tail]`) is gone from all four copies: `declaredMemberEntry` (every door gate: where, dimension, include, related-column, field-read admission, preview column map, record-currency, structured-JSON dimension door), `NativeSQLStrategy.lookupMember`, `lookupCubeMember` (= `ObjectQLStrategy.lookupMember`), and `measureEntryOf`. Read in the head: `relationshipMembers` gets `declared: false` for `vendor.region`, so `assertDimensionJoinsBacked` refuses the undeclared path with the existing `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 "traverses relationship path 'vendor'" envelope, and `assertRelationshipColumnsExist` refuses a declared path to a column the related object lacks. This is card Work item 1 and seat ruling 2 as written.
2. **Flat-key arm restricted — right.** `pathOf(flatEntry) === member` (with the `$` sigil stripped). The dataset compiler writes `sql: d.field` verbatim (dataset-compiler.ts L879), so a dataset dimension `supplier_region` over `supplier.region` still answers that spelling, as does the skill's `account_industry: { sql: 'account.industry' }` (dashboards.md L451); one over a base column (`vendor_region` over `region`) no longer answers `vendor.region`. Nothing in the package mints a flat key: `inferCubeFromQuery` mints dotted members verbatim, and `bindDatasetFiltersToObjectFields` mints `KEY__object_field` keys, which no dotted spelling flattens to. Card Work item 2, seat ruling 3.
3. **One rule, no drift — right.** Gate and both strategies read the same function (seat ruling 4); `measureEntryOf` keeps #20912's own-keys-only guard by re-checking `hasOwnProperty` on the returned key. The undeclared `split('.')[1]` / `slice(1)` fallbacks in native `resolveFieldSql`, `resolveDimensionSql`, `resolveStorageTarget` and objectql `resolveCubeFieldName` now return the member itself; read in the head, they were unreachable for a dotted member, because `lookupMember(…, 'dimension')` answers every dotted member (a declared key, or the synthetic traversal) before them.
4. **Own qualifier includes the bare object — right.** A compiled dataset's cube is `sql: dataset.object` (dataset-compiler.ts L955) and named for the dataset, so `OBJECT.region` is a second spelling of the same base table, not a relationship hop. It is pinned on `main` by the #28258 CONTROL ("'OBJECT.region', which resolves to the declared 'region', still serves on every face"), by `previewWhereColumns` (#28691) and by the include gate's own jsdoc. No pin moves.
5. **No public surface — right.** `cube-member-key.ts` is not exported from `src/index.ts` (unchanged); no error code, status or envelope is added; every refusal reuses `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 or the engine's existing cross-object refusal.
6. **Tests — right.** Eight pins in the existing real-SQLite harness, on both live strategies: the three Done-when outcomes (never the base column; CUBE.region / OBJECT.region still the base column; related column through a declared include, or refusal), plus the flat-key pair and the hand-authored cube pair. No existing test edited.
7. **Not fully retired, no contract effect (see ④).** Objectql `resolveStorageTarget` (L1892) still carries `member.split('.').slice(1).join('.')` where the native twin was changed; `resolveMeasureAggregation` (L1944) and `assertMeasureFields`'s `stripPrefix` (analytics-service.ts L4265) read a MEASURE by its tail whatever the prefix. Both are behind `mintableMeasureKey` (#5918), which refuses any dotted non-qualifier measure on both mint paths, and measures have no traversal tier, so no input reaches them wrongly.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-analytics: patch`, `!` in the title, BREAKING banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker — `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — and both declaration lines line-initial in the changeset and the PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches AGENTS.md ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). `Clause-②:` arm right: an input that was answered (`vendor.region` over a vendor with no `region`, served from the base column on `main`) is now refused, so the accept set shrinks; the "argue `no` with no arm" branch of seat ruling 5 does not apply because not every such input resolves to a related field. `Metadata-protocol: none` right: no key, value or type an author writes in a cube or dataset changes; the input that moves is a query-time member spelling. The remedy stands in prose (spell it `CUBE.region` or `region`; a stored member is not rewritten); the gate's own source (`scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, branch 1 "label convention") refuses a `FROM`/`TO` label beside `no-migration-prescription`, and `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag 1 — keep `OBJECT.region` as an own qualifier beside `CUBE.region`: ACCEPTED, option A.** Seat ruling 2 names the cube's own name; its intent (the first segment names the cube's own table, never a relation) is met by both spellings, since the object `cube.sql` reads is the base table itself. Option B would refuse an input the card never touched and rewrite two existing controls (#28258, #28691): a wider narrowing than the card. Answered, not escalated.
- **Dev flag 2 — internal name `declaredCubeMemberKey` / `cube-member-key.ts`: ACCEPTED.** Package-internal, not exported; the name states the rule.
- **Deviation — file surface adds `cube-member-key.ts` and `structured-json-dimension-door.ts`: ACCEPTED.** Seat ruling 4 asks for one shared helper, which is the new module; `measureEntryOf` was a fourth copy of the bare-tail rule, and leaving it would be the drift ruling 4 forbids. Both stay inside `packages/services/service-analytics/src`; no `packages/spec/**`, no `ui/**`.
- **Deviation — changeset remedy as prose instead of a FROM / TO line: ACCEPTED**, for the reason in ②; the prose names both the input that moves and the two spellings that replace it.
- **open_questions 1 and 2:** answered above (A and A).
- **out_of_scope (a)** — a CUBE-qualified MEASURE in a dataset `where` (`DATASET.total`) is read by the gate as the measure but compiled by both strategies as a hop named for the dataset: pre-existing on `main` (the dimension lookup's synthetic tier preempts the measure bag in the same order before and after this PR). Not moved here; follow-up card.
- **out_of_scope (b)** — a hand-authored cube (no include gate) on the native strategy answers `DATABASE_ERROR` / 500 for a related column the related object lacks, where the dataset door answers `INVALID_FIELD` / 400. Pre-existing for `vendor.nope` on `main`; this PR routes `vendor.region` into the same class (the join tier) instead of serving it from the wrong column, which is the card's Done-when ("filters the related field … or refuses"). The 400 / 500 parity on the hand-authored path is a follow-up card, not a finding against this head.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** The spec publishes a member as `CUBE.KEY` (analytics.zod.ts L674/L678; references/data/analytics.mdx L129/L130) and a member's `sql` as "a field of the cube's object or a relationship path ending in one (`account.industry`)"; data-modeling/analytics.mdx L248 says related fields are reached "by dotted path … only declared" relationships. Nowhere does the spec declare that `ANYTHING.KEY` names `KEY`. So the narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer: a dotted member whose first segment is neither the cube nor its object was always, under the published spec, a relationship path, and the PR makes the spec's own refusal (#28258's include gate, #28558's related-column gate) real for it. The `legacy second-segment` arm existed only in the strategies' private jsdoc. No implementation gap is narrowed at the consumer: the related-field read through a declared include is delivered (pin 3, pin 6, pin 7), and the undeclared path is refused by the gate that already existed for every other dotted member.

**Trying to break it (read in the head, not run):**
- Multi-hop `a.b.c`: tail `b.c`, flat `a_b_c` must carry `sql: 'a.b.c'` — same as the old `rest.join('.')`. Holds.
- `$`-sigil `sql`: `pathOf` strips it before comparing. Holds.
- A `cube.sql` that is not a bare identifier (a SELECT): the object arm never matches, `cube.name` still does. Holds.
- Inherited keys (`constructor`): `bag[member]` truthiness is inherited from the old code in the gate and both strategies (unchanged), and `measureEntryOf` re-checks `hasOwnProperty`, so #20912's own-keys-only contract on the structured-JSON door is kept. Holds.
- The three faces agree: the preview path runs `assertDimensionJoinsBacked` / `assertRelationshipColumnsExist` / `assertPreviewJoinsNothing` before the evaluator and reads `previewWhereColumns` / `previewEvaluationCube` through the same `declaredMemberEntry`, so a `vendor.region` runtimeFilter is refused on the draft preview too. Holds by reading.
- A cube or object whose name equals a lookup field name on that object (`vendor` cube over a `vendor` lookup): the own qualifier wins and `vendor.region` names the base field. This is the published `CUBE.KEY` semantics, unchanged by this PR; not a finding.

**Findings:**
1. **nit** — objectql `resolveStorageTarget` keeps the `member.split('.').slice(1).join('.')` fallback that its native twin dropped (objectql-strategy.ts L1892). Unreachable for a dotted member (`lookupMember(…, 'dimension')` answers every dotted one first), so no effect on correctness or the contract; the two copies now disagree in text only. Follow-up or accepted deviation.
2. **nit** — the helper's jsdoc claims to be "the ONE rule … for every reader in this package that resolves one", while `resolveMeasureAggregation`'s alias arm (L1944) and `assertMeasureFields`'s `stripPrefix` (L4265) still read a measure by its tail. Both sit behind `mintableMeasureKey` (#5918), which refuses every dotted non-qualifier measure on both mint paths, so no input reaches them wrongly; the claim is overstated, the behaviour is not. Not a prose face; accepted deviation or follow-up.
3. **nit** (prose face, changeset) — the `Clause-②:` sentence lists "an `order` key" among the narrowed positions. An `order` key is an output alias gated by `assertOrderKeysSelected` and emitted as `"MEMBER"` by `orderClauseSql`; it is never resolved by this rule. It inherits the narrowing only through the selected spelling it must match, so the effect is right and the wording loose. Fixable on the changeset alone.
4. **nit** — the new pins cover the two live strategies the card asks for; the preview face (which the #28258 harness also drives) is not pinned for the new inputs. Reading shows the same gates run before the evaluator; a pin would cost one case per outcome. Follow-up.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.
